the entire month has been an excessive string of good deeds that I never believed myself capable of. And it all comes down to driving.

There were two grand "Missions of LOVE" as our circle of friends is calling them recently. For the past year we were planning to rescue this one friend of ours from the middle of nowhere village he was living in in Canada. Now we were pouncing on the opportunity. One of my pals drove alllll the way across Niagara Falls, up a peninsula, boarded a ferry, crossed freaking Lake Huron, drove deep into the island they landed on, and picked him up... then turned right around and came all the way back. No rest.

I wasn't expecting the journey to be THAT daunting. I wasn't expecting it to almost total his car, either! The rough road conditions almost snapped the right front wheel right off the hub! It lost two lugs!

My part of the plan was simply to take my friend's girlfriend (who lives near me) with me over to upstate New York so they could meet and spend the Fourth of July together with our other pal (because 'MURRIKUHH), and then take them all back to Massachusetts with me.

Well, as it turns out, another friend of mine from Massachusetts was going to be visiting our pal in New York, and they were swiftly becoming an item. After seeing what New York Pal had gone through, I told him, "Don't worry about <her>. I'll bring her all the way here for you."--even though she lives out on the cape, and that's about 200 miles in the wrong direction, BAH WHO CARES! I was inspired! The risk he took for our other friends was too great to go unacknowledged. So after I brought couple #1 back from New York and delivered them safely to their abode, I rested up and paced myself and prepared for the GRAND JOURNEY that would begin on July 16th.

On that date, I set off at 1pm and managed to get all the way to the cape by 4 on the DOT. I expected far worse traffic than I got! She didn't get out of work until 6:30 pm and frankly I was piss broke so I couldn't even go and enjoy the sights... just sat there and waited until we could load up the car and get rolling.

It took us until 3 am due to a) getting food at the best freaking barbecue place I have ever known(if you're in MA, or even Connecticut or Rhode Island, DO check out BT's Smokehouse in Sturbridge! It's SENSATIONAL!). and b) stopping to rest and stretch our legs just about at Syracuse. I gravely underestimated NY Pal's hospitality and gratitude. They kept me an additional day and a half just to make sure I got rested enough, and sent me home with gas money and enough extra dough to ensure that my cell phone can actually stay on! Warm fuzzy feelings abound. But that wasn't what was crazy.

What was crazy was doing it YET AGAIN on the 21st. It mucked up the remainder of my entire week, but I understood that she needed to get back, even though all of us were rooting for her to stay with him! Sometimes, though, you just can't push things too fast. This makes three times I've put a thousand miles on my car for the benefit of my friends and nearly died a few times falling asleep at the wheel... Really I should've >_> I distinctly remember waking up more than TWICE in the far right lane cruising slow behind some other relatively slow car. How I didn't hit anything was a miracle.

But the thing that made it so worthwhile for me was that it was about bringing people together so they could be happy. Even when I was taking her back to the cape, I knew it was an installment toward some greater union in the future. They know what they want now, and the absence will only make hearts grow fonder. There's a lot of stuff in the air but now I actually feel like I've contributed, finally. I've given them some stability. My friends know, if they need me, all they must do is call. And I'll be there, every time.

No paying job I've ever held has made me feel as worthwhile as that.
